artifacts.summary: Widened run_post_deploy_reconcile_pass() in redeploy-checkpoint-lib.sh to a lock-gated, scope-tagged system-wide deploy-pending sweep; corrected regeneration-is-manual-only.md's sanctioned-sites prose to match the lint; 17-case fixture suite proves fail-before/pass-after, stale-tree refusal, lock guard, reporting scope, and the demotion-risk negative control.

completion_data.completion_summary: Widened the Inter-Cycle Redeploy Checkpoint's existing post-deploy reconcile pass (scripts/lib/redeploy-checkpoint-lib.sh) to sweep specs/state.json system-wide for any deploy-pending task, lock-gated and reporting-scoped, closing the gap where a task refused by the completion-deploy gate in an earlier cycle stayed invisible to the self-heal mechanism unless a later invocation named it again. No new deploy-trigger call site added; the completion-deploy gate itself is unchanged and still refuses against a genuinely stale tree. Also corrected context/patterns/regeneration-is-manual-only.md's sanctioned-sites prose to match test-lint-deploy-caller-wrap.sh's mechanical census.

memory_candidates.content: When widening an existing self-heal/promotion mechanism from invocation-scoped to system-wide (e.g. /orchestrate's post-deploy reconcile pass), a naive 'not already in the invocation's own selected set' predicate is NOT sufficient to scope the widening to genuinely out-of-batch candidates. A task that IS a member of the current invocation's own task/batch list, but was deliberately excluded THIS SAME cycle for a real reason (a dependent operation failed, or a self-attribution/ownership screen withheld it), still matches a naive disk-state predicate and gets silently re-included by the widened sweep, defeating that same-cycle decision. The correct additional exclusion is: a swept candidate must be a member of neither the original selected set NOR the invocation's full batch list (not just the narrower selected subset). Caught by running the existing regression suite for the unmodified mechanism (not just new fixture cases for the new one) -- two negative-control arms (a dependency-failure arm and a withholding/self-attribution arm) both regressed under the naive predicate and both passed once the full-batch-membership exclusion was added.

Adding a new scripts/tests/*.sh file to this repo's agent-system extension source store requires a companion one-line registration in that extension's manifest.json provides.scripts array (via scripts/sync-manifest-scripts.sh --write, run from the DEPLOYED .claude/scripts/ copy of that script, not the source store -- it enforces deploy-root-guard.sh). A missing entry produces no authoring-time signal; it only surfaces later as a check-extension-docs.sh Rule Q FAIL ('script file on disk NOT in provides.scripts'), which verify-deploy.sh's doc-lint gate then reports. Similarly, editing any context/ doc tracked in index-entries.json changes its line count, which generate-context-line-counts.sh --write must re-derive (Rule R), or verify-deploy.sh's gate3 reports a line_count mismatch. Both are one-line, mechanical, deploy-state-INDEPENDENT companion edits (unlike ordinary content-drift findings, which clear only on redeploy) -- worth fixing proactively during implementation even when the file isn't in the task's own declared file_scope.
